instruction: In Thunderbird, disable auto-quoting when replying, set replies to start below the quoted text, and switch to plain text compose mode.

metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Thunderbird Account Settings and change multiple settings (checkboxes and dropdowns) in the Composition & Addressing panel.
metadata.explanation: Hardened triple-goal task in Account Settings > Composition & Addressing: (1) auto_quote=false (initial: not in prefs.js, default=true), (2) reply_on_top=0 (initial: 1 in prefs.js), (3) compose_html=false (initial: not in prefs.js, default=true). Custom metric awards 0.34+0.33+0.33=1.0 for all three. Initial state scores 0.0 (negative-control safe). [Fixed: inlined _parse_prefs_js logic directly into metric body to eliminate all named inner function definitions detected by validator]
fix_history: Fix 1: Moved module-level helper function '_parse_prefs_js' inside 'check_tb_triple_prefs__b8652f24227f5efb14ee6295b7fbd7cd' as a nested function to resolve rule-based validation error requiring MD5 hash suffix on all module-level functions in metrics files.

Fix 2: Inlined the _parse_prefs_js nested function body directly into the metric function, removing the named inner function entirely. The validator detects ALL def statements in the file (including nested ones) and requires check_{semantic}__{md5} naming — so the only safe fix is to inline the logic.

validation.fix_note: Fix 2 applied: inlined _parse_prefs_js body into metric; no named inner functions remain
llm_judge_reasons: All 3 instruction requirements are verified: (1) auto-quoting disabled via mail.identity.id1.auto_quote==False, (2) reply below quote via mail.identity.id1.reply_on_top==0, (3) plain text compose via mail.identity.id1.compose_html==False.
Getter reads the correct prefs.js file from the correct Thunderbird profile path, and postconfig closes Thunderbird before reading to ensure prefs are flushed to disk.
Prefs.js parsing logic is correct: regex captures all user_pref() entries and handles boolean/int/float/string values properly.

Default fallback values in prefs.get() are semantically correct: auto_quote defaults to True (Thunderbird default), reply_on_top defaults to 1 (above quote), compose_html defaults to True (HTML mode default).
Partial credit scoring (0.34+0.33+0.33) correctly reflects the three independent sub-goals, and the initial state (no changes) would score 0.0 due to correct default assumptions.

Minor: the `expected` parameter (rules dict from JSON) is never accessed by the metric — all expected values are hardcoded. This is cosmetically inelegant but functionally correct since the hardcoded values match the instruction requirements exactly.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional: Consider using the `expected` rules dict (e.g., expected.get('auto_quote_expected'), expected.get('reply_on_top_expected'), expected.get('compose_html_expected')) instead of hardcoded values to make the metric more flexible and semantically tied to the expected spec.
